products.method_and_provenance: Methodology page (initial publication 24 Jul 2026; PDF /ocpi_methodology.pdf): OCPI = volume-weighted winsorized mean of executed on-demand rental prices per GPU type over a rolling one-hour window; every trade retained, outliers clipped at unpublished symmetric percentile bounds α/(1-α) drawn from the volume-weighted empirical CDF; no smoothing; precision $0.001; eligibility = verified counterparties (wash-trade screen), trade finality (realized prices only, no offers), no minimum size, provider reliability/re-verification (CUDA, VRAM, PCIe etc. thresholds shared only with regulators). Sources: ~150 partnered providers/operators/lessors, ~1,000 transactions/day, majority US volume, invoice-level records; on-demand only. Thin windows carry forward last value (Market Disruption Event fallback hierarchy). Governance: Oversight Committee 3–5 members majority independent, IOSCO-referenced, information barriers between benchmark function and Ornn's commercial/rental business, no restatements except falsification/material error, dated changelog. Freshness shown as 'Updated <date> at 20:00 UTC' and 'As of <date> · settled daily at 4:00 PM ET · OCPI methodology'; each page repeats 'volume-weighted, winsorized average of transacted GPU rental prices… listed on Bloomberg'. API fields: index_value, last_updated/date, region ('' or 'global'), access:'public-3mo'.

products.name: Ornn Data — GPU Forward Curves (published forward marks by tenor)
products.operator: Ornn Data LLC (Ornn AI, Inc.); marks assembled by Ornn's analyst team
products.audience: Premium ($500/mo) and Full subscribers: institutional traders/operators hedging compute, lenders underwriting GPU-backed financing, buyers timing term contracts, providers pricing long-dated capacity; also consumed internally by the Payback Period analytics
products.data_model: Unit: USD per GPU-hour term price (flat rate over the contract) with an alternative 'implied forward' basis (marginal rate between neighbouring tenors, obtained by differencing cumulative cost = price × months). Tenors (5, discrete): 1M (1 month), 6M (6), 1Y (12), 3Y (36), 5Y (60) — axis labels '1 mo / 6 mo / 12 mo / 36 mo / 60 mo'. Tracked curves (9): H100 SXM, H200, A100 SXM4, RTX 5090, B200, RTX PRO 6000 WS, B300, GB200, GB300; only curves with ≥1 valid mark appear in `data`, fully unmarked ones (e.g. GB200) in `suppressed`; website catalog shows all nine with a dash for each missing mark. No interpolation, carry-forward or default fill in the data ('a missing tenor remains a gap'). Region: global. Update cadence: 'updated weekly' (glossary); marks are hand-published asynchronously — `as_of_date`/`asOf` = per-mark edit/publish timestamp in UTC, explicitly 'not the market observation time'; no historical marks via API ('current marks only'). Public evidence of levels (Ornn paper, Sep 2026, marks of 13 Aug 2026 for A100/H100/H200/B200 and 1 Sep 2026 for B300) as % of each family's 1M term price — 6M/1Y/3Y/5Y: A100 95.0/93.1/84.2/80.2; H100 95.0/86.2/68.2/59.8; H200 92.4/80.2/51.0/43.7; B200 99.1/97.9/69.1/53.8; B300 93.8/81.3/60.9/53.8; implied forward months 37–60 as % of 1M: 74/47/33/31/43. Announced 30 Jun 2026 for H100, H200, B200; GB200/GB300 added later as products.
functionality: Routes: /analytics/gpu/forward ('Forward Curves Table — Every forward curve at a glance'), /analytics/gpu/forward/{slug} ('{GPU} Forward — Implied future compute price'), /analytics/forward-curves ('Published forward marks by tenor'; search keywords forward, curve, futures, tenor, marks, term structure, contango, backwardation, strip)

products.method_and_provenance: FAQ/glossary: 'Curves are sourced from active deals in the market, assembled by our team of analysts, and updated weekly'; each mark carries provenance (source type, edit/publish timestamp, sample count when supplied). Term price = flat rate over contract; implied forward = differenced cumulative cost between tenors (example given: $2.10 at 1Y and $1.46 at 3Y implies $1.14 for years 2–3); ladders whose cumulative cost fails to rise are rejected, not published. X article (30 Jun 2026): curve 'replaces a forecast with an observable signal'; 'Because compute cannot be stored, the curve reflects expected scarcity rather than a cost of carry'. OCPI methodology explicitly excludes forward/reserved contracts from the spot index, so the forward curve is a separate analyst-marked product, not derived from transactions in the same way. Caution: search-engine summaries attach Silicon Data's language ('zero to 36 months', '0.25-month grid', 'no-arbitrage forward rates') to Ornn; Ornn's own docs state five discrete tenors to 60 months and no interpolation.
products.visual_design: Live chart is behind the login wall; design reconstructed from the app bundle and two public renderings. App chart (lightweight-charts): transparent background, text colour --chart-text (rgba(255,255,255,0.6) dark / rgba(11,11,12,0.62) light), font var(--font-title) = PP Neue Montreal; horizontal gridlines in --chart-grid (#ffffff0d), vertical grid off; x-axis is a hidden time scale (months mapped to timestamps from 2026-01-01 at 2,630,016 s/month, fixLeftEdge/fixRightEdge, library ticks blanked) with app-drawn labels '1 mo, 6 mo, 12 mo, 36 mo, 60 mo' spaced ≥44px; right price scale with 10% margins; crosshair 1px dashed --chart-crosshair, vertical label hidden, horizontal label on --chart-line background; series = AreaSeries per GPU, lineColor from the GPU colour (all defined #FFFFFF then themed to --chart-line, comparison series take the palette), lineWidth 2 for the first curve and 1 for others, line styles cycling Solid/Dashed/Dotted/LargeDashed, fill --chart-area-top→bottom only for a single curve, circle markers size 0.6 at tenors, crosshair marker radius 5, no last-value label or price line; scroll/zoom disabled; canvas fades in (opacity transition var(--dur-stage)). Public rendering on /publications (Figure 5 SVG, viewBox 320×208): y gridlines at 40/60/80/100 (currentColor, 0.5px, opacity .25), x ticks 1M 6M 1Y 3Y 5Y on a log-spaced axis, axis caption 'Term price as % of the 1-month mark' (8.5px, opacity .55), lead series A100 SXM4 solid 1.75px in --text-primary, other four 1px at opacity .6 with dash patterns '5 3' (H100 SXM), '2 3' (H200), '7 3 2 3' (B200), '1 4' (B300), end-of-line value labels 80 (lead, weight 500), 60, 44, 54; all figure text in var(--font-numbers) 8px with letter-spacing var(--tracking-numbers). Paper Figure 5 axes: x 'Contract tenor (months, log scale)', y 'Term price as % of 1-month mark' (40–100), five family series. Also found in the bundle: a decorative SVG of stacked forward-curve lines (data-mark='forward-curve-line', stroke var(--chart-line), stroke-width 1.3, opacities 0.21–0.34) used as a monochrome motif.
strengths: Explicit dual basis (term vs implied forward) with the arithmetic published and validation that rejects non-monotone ladders
Honest gap handling: null never shown as 0.00, suppressed curves listed, per-mark provenance and publish timestamps, 'not the market observation time' disclaimer
Covers five discrete tenors out to 5 years and nine SKUs including B300/GB200/GB300 that have no spot index
Integrated with payback/depreciation analytics and with the spot index on the same platform and API
Announced publicly (X article 30 Jun 2026) and evidenced in a first-party paper with a normalized figure, so shape/retention can be checked without a subscription
weaknesses: Fully paywalled ($500/mo Premium minimum); no public chart or even a catalog preview outside the /publications figure and the paper
Marks are analyst-entered ('hand_entered_mark') from 'active deals', weekly, with no published sample counts, dealer list, or methodology document comparable to the OCPI one; not transaction-settled
Only current marks — no history of the curve via API, so curve evolution cannot be tracked by subscribers programmatically
Only five tenors; the smooth line between marks is display interpolation and could be misread as data
Publish timestamp rather than observation time; weekly cadence lags a spot index that settles daily
Coverage gaps acknowledged (GB200 cited as an example of a fully unmarked curve)

cross_cutting: Unit convention is universal: USD per GPU-hour, normalised per card (GetDeploying: 'an 8×H100 instance at $40/hr counts as $5.00'; Computable: '$68.80 for an 8-GPU instance normalizes to $8.60/GPU-hour'). Only the level indices (GetDeploying Jan-2025=100, GPU Tracker Feb-2026=100, GPUAlpha 148.72) depart from it, and each says explicitly it is 'a level, not a price'.

Every index page states constituents/coverage and cadence above or beside the chart: Silicon Data '95% neo-cloud / 100% hyperscalers / 80% of market', 'once per business day'; SemiAnalysis 'hyperscale clouds, neoclouds, GPU marketplaces, and rental routers/aggregators', 'published hourly'; Ornn 'from executed trades', 'settles once per trading day at 4:00 PM ET'; Computable '29 providers through 31 collector sources', 'every 15 minutes'; GetDeploying '81 providers and 103 GPU models', weekly; GPU Tracker '54+ providers', 'every 6 hours'.

Spot/on-demand dominates; committed tenors are rare and shown as ranges or separate products: SemiAnalysis is the only public grid (On-Demand, 1y*, 18m*, 2y*, 3y*, 4y*, 5y* with '25% prepay'), Silicon Data sells a 1–36-month implied forward curve, Ornn sells 'forward marks by tenor', Compute Desk's headline tickers are 'US 1Y rental', Compute Exchange quotes 1/3/6/12/24/36-month terms privately, AIMultiple/GetDeploying show 1-year (and 3-year) reserved list-price discounts (~31% / ~50%). Survey-based contract data is always a 25th–75th percentile range, never a point.

Neo-cloud vs hyperscaler is the recurring segment split: Silicon Data publishes separate readings ($2.66 vs $7.20 H100), SemiAnalysis over-weights hyperscalers in its composite, GetDeploying quantifies an '88%' hyperscaler premium, Ornn scopes to 'the neocloud market', Computable tags Oracle as a separate 'hyperscaler' source class never seated on a panel.

Three provenance classes never converge and each vendor argues for its own: listed/scraped prices (Silicon Data, Computable, GetDeploying, GPU Tracker, AIMultiple, GPUAlpha), executed transactions (Ornn 'listed prices are not prices', Compute Desk 'private compute transactions'), and analyst surveys (SemiAnalysis '100+ market participants'). Same-day H100 prints on 2026-09-15/16 ranged from $2.53 (Ornn trades, Silicon Data FAQ) to $2.66 (Silicon Data card) to $3.50–3.51 (GPU Tracker p25, Computable); the TechFlow comparison piece notes indices 'don't converge'.

Robustness devices are the differentiator and are named in the methodology text: one price per provider per period (SemiAnalysis, GetDeploying 'one vote, not eight'), winsorization (Ornn), interquantile/central-third mean (Computable), median-of-medians (GetDeploying, AIMultiple), p25 rather than min (GPU Tracker), circuit breakers and forward-fill (SemiAnalysis), jump screens with corroboration (Computable), basis adjustment for term/geography/CPU/variant (Silicon Data).

No-revision policies are becoming standard where settlement is intended: Ornn 'history is never silently restated', Computable 'Published observations are never revised… Corrections publish forward under a new version', GetDeploying splices out its own data corrections; SemiAnalysis only says parameters 'may be refined over time'; Silicon Data publishes nothing on revisions.

Terminal and exchange distribution is the credibility signal: Bloomberg tickers SDH100RT/SDA100RT/SDB200RT/SDLLMTK (Silicon Data), SAH100SC (SemiAnalysis), ORNNH100 (Ornn), Refinitiv + Bloomberg (Compute Desk); futures on CME/NYMEX (Silicon Data, 5 Oct 2026, 'a month's worth of rent' per contract), ICE (Ornn, cash-settled USD) and Nodal (Compute Desk). Settlement use of the index is separately licensed everywhere (Silicon Data 'settlement reference is licensed separately', Computable LICENSE-DATA §2).

Freemium gating pattern: latest value plus a short free window (Silicon Data 30 days history; Ornn 'three months of daily history for 5 GPUs'; SemiAnalysis H100 only), full history/hourly grain/API/CSV paid (Silicon Data Pro $998/month; Ornn Premium $500/month, Full custom); open-source and indie trackers are fully free but non-commercial or ad-supported.

Freshness is displayed as a stamp or delta badge rather than a constituent view: 'Updated September 15, 2026 at 20:00 UTC' (Ornn), 'AS OF WED SEP 16 14:45 UTC' (Computable), 'Last updated Sept. 14, 2026' (GetDeploying), 'Live Index · Updated 2026-04-19' (GPU Tracker, stale), '% vs 7D' (Silicon Data), period labels 'Apr 2026' (SemiAnalysis). Only Computable shows the individual constituent prices, weights and source URLs behind a print; Ornn shows a 14-day settle table; Silicon Data and SemiAnalysis show no constituent-level data.

Design language converges on Next.js + Tailwind dashboards, dark-first or dark-capable, with a sans body and a monospace numeral font (Fragment Mono at Silicon Data and Compute Desk, JetBrains Mono at Compute Exchange/GetDeploying/GPU Tracker, Geist Mono at Ornn/Computable landing, IBM Plex Mono at Computable market, Roboto Mono at AIMultiple), one saturated accent (cyan #67def9, amber #f7b041, lime #a3e635, green #176e4a/#00dd88, orange #ff4d00), Recharts or nivo charts, range-button groups ('1W 1M 3M 1Y ALL', '24H 7D 30D 90D'), toggle pills for GPU/tenor/segment placed directly above the chart, and up/down-arrow delta badges ('vs 7D', '1D', '24h/7d/30d').

Charts are client-rendered everywhere (fetched HTML shows 'Loading latest pricing…', 'No chart data available', 'Building the index...'), so the public tables and FAQ prose carry the verifiable numbers; the tables are the de-facto API for readers without a subscription.

Governance disclosure scales with settlement ambition: Ornn (Oversight Committee 3–5 members, contributor code of conduct, 5-year records, MDE fallback) and Computable (GOVERNANCE.md, versioned parameters, coverage bands 98%/90%) publish formal governance; Compute Desk claims IOSCO/BMR compliance without documents; Silicon Data, SemiAnalysis and the indie trackers publish none.

USD in U.S. regions' (Thunder).

products.name: SF Compute (San Francisco Compute) market + orderbook
products.audience: AI labs and teams buying node-blocks of H100/H200/B200/B300/GB300 for hours to years; tenants reselling reserved capacity; API/CLI-first engineers ("No dashboards to learn").
products.data_model: Unit is dollars per node-hour where "1 node is 8 GPUs" (CLI prints "RATE (PER 8X GPU NODE) $20.00/node/hr", list view column "RATE ($/NODE/HR, 8x GPU)"); marketing converts to $/gpu/hr ("$2.03 average gpu/hr", "Reserved price $3.00/gpu/hr", "Realized price $4.29/gpu/hr"). Hardware unit = SKU (fungibility boundary; properties accelerator, region, availability_zone, rdma_type, form factor), e.g. "sea-3-h100 8 x H100 80GB HBM3 2,016 GiB 1.5 TiB 56 vCPU", "iad-12-h200 8 x H200 141GB HBM3e"; quickstart SKUs ams-1-h100, iad-2-h100, ord-1-a100, sea-3-h100, nrt-1-h100; orderbook example also prices B200 and H200; H100/B300/GB300 clusters by contract. Tenor: any delivery window [start_at, end_at) aligned to whole minutes; fills in whole minutes, minimum 1 node for 1 minute; site says contracts "from one node for one hour to thousands of nodes for multiple years". Orderbook per SKU, anonymized; /windows enumerates SKU x window combos with duration_hours, total_bid_order_count, total_ask_order_count, best_bid, best_ask; /quote = top of book; /depth default 20 levels, cap 100 per side; /fills default 7 days back, max 30 days; order history capped at 30 days. Zones: Amsterdam, Ashburn, Chicago, Seattle, Tokyo (from SKU prefixes). Cadence: trading engine matches continuously; no timestamp on the homepage average.
functionality: Public homepage stat "$2.03 average gpu/hr" and resale explainer with stacked-area chart (x axis "Wk 2 … Wk 12", y axis "GPU-hours"; legend "Reserved (3 mo) $302,400", "Resale revenue", "Burst at 1.5x", "Burst at 4.5x", "Spot at 0.5x"; callouts "Realized price $4.29/gpu/hr", "43%", "Reserved price $3.00/gpu/hr")

CLI order entry: sf orders create --side buy|sell --pool --count <nodes> --start now|<time> --duration 1h|--stop "in 1h" --max-rate <$/node-hr> (or --max-price total) / --min-rate; --allow-standing (rest on book) ; --allow-partial; --sku pin or interactive SKU picker; quickstart shows a "NEXT 48H" availability sparkline
Order statuses pending / filled / partially_filled / standing / cancelled / rejected; default immediate-or-cancel; standing orders keep matching over the un-elapsed remainder of their window

Orderbook API (public preview): GET /preview/v2/orderbook/windows | /quote | /depth | /fills with ?requirements=accelerator:h100;availability_zone:a filters; responses give dollars_per_node_hour and allocation_schedule_delta segments

Reselling: sell back unused time; realized-price arithmetic table ("Net compute cost = Purchase cost − resale credits after fees", "Realized discount = Resale credits after fees ÷ purchase cost × 100%"); interactive CapacityChart in docs showing gross vs net allocation with standing-sell bands
SKU availability schedule endpoints ("purchasable-capacity schedule of every SKU"), estimate-an-order endpoint
Products: VMs, bare metal, managed Slurm; status pill "All systems normal"; Specs page FAQ (refunds for failed nodes, InfiniBand on BM/Slurm, VMs Q3 2026)
products.method_and_provenance: Prices are limit prices on a continuous double-auction order book per SKU and window; buyers/sellers set rates in $/node-hour. Top of book, depth (orders at same rate+SKU collapse to one level; bids descending, asks ascending) and fills ("each fill records the nodes and price that actually traded") are exposed via API; "Orderbook responses never expose participant, pool, or capacity identity". Sell-side platform fee = fixed fee per node-hour x node-hours sold + percentage x sale value, org-specific and changeable, estimated in the CLI before confirm; buy orders carry no fee. Holds reserve worst-case credits. Homepage "$2.03 average gpu/hr" states no window or weighting. Docs cite a "September 9, 2026 resale article" reporting a "25% average realized discount". The market UI itself (sfcompute.com/dashboard) is behind WorkOS AuthKit login, and the docs page "How the market works" redirects to a gated blueprint.sfcompute.com host.

cross_cutting: Unit fragmentation: $/GPU-hr (Vast per offer, Prime Intellect, io.net, Akash, RunPod, Together), $/node-hr with an 8-GPU node (SF Compute), $/instance-hr (CoreWeave). Only SF Compute ("1 node is 8 GPUs") and CoreWeave (GPU Count column) make the conversion explicit; a benchmark page must normalise and label the tier/config.

Published term ladders are short and stop at 6-12 months: Together 7-30 / 31-90 / 91-180 / 181+ days with prices; Vast 1 / 3 / 6 months ("Up to 50% Off", no numbers); RunPod savings plans 3 / 6 months plus a 1mo/3mo/6mo/12mo/12mo+ reserved grid that is entirely "Contact sales"; CoreWeave "up to 60%" with no tenors; SF Compute is the only one with arbitrary forward windows (minute-aligned). Everything beyond ~6 months routes to sales.

Marketplaces pair price with availability counts; vendors do not: Akash shows total/available GPUs and providers, io.net total/hired/idle, Prime Intellect "Available:" counts and stockStatus, Vast offer count/verification/reliability; RunPod, Together and CoreWeave show no availability on the page (console or sales only).

The API carries a richer statistic than the page shows: Akash API returns min/max/avg/weightedAverage/med but the page prints only "Price (Starting at)"; Vast's API exposes every offer while the pricing page shows one card value with unstated statistic; SF Compute exposes top-of-book, depth and fills but the homepage prints one "average gpu/hr"; io.net returns five product-specific prices per hardware but the Trending table shows one "Price" column.

Freshness is rarely stated: only RunPod stamps the page ("Updated September 13, 2026"); Together dates a promo ("valid until 09/30/26"); SF Compute and Prime Intellect say "realtime"/continuous; Akash and io.net rely on live APIs with no visible timestamp; CoreWeave and Vast show none.

Quality and trust proxies sit next to price on marketplaces: Vast reliability %, DLPerf and verified tier; Akash provider uptime (7-day) and audited providers; io.net connectivity tiers 1-4 and verified/staked devices; Prime Intellect Secure vs Community cloud and provisioningTime; SF Compute vetted SKUs and refunds for failed nodes. Vendor rate cards use no such column.

Interruptible/spot appears as a parallel column at roughly 40-55% of on-demand wherever shown: Together H100 $1.99 vs $3.99, H200 $2.99 vs $5.99, B200 $4.09 vs $8.19; CoreWeave HGX H100 $19.71 vs $49.24, B200 $34.11 vs $68.80; Vast H100 SXM min_bid median $1.73 vs ask median $3.14; SF Compute's resale illustration assumes "Spot at 0.5x".

Committed vs realized framing exists only at SF Compute (realized price after resale, "25% average realized discount") — no other product distinguishes the contracted rate from the effective rate after resale, promo or savings plan.

Charts are scarce; tables dominate. Only SF Compute (stacked-area resale chart, price-ladder diagrams), io.net (daily compute-hours bars), Akash stats (USD-spent time series) and Vast (30D/90D per-GPU history cards) draw anything; no product in the cluster publishes a public historical $/GPU-hr curve with stated constituents.

Two funnel archetypes: marketplaces use a pick-config → compare-offers flow (Prime Intellect "1 Choose GPU → 2 Compare Offers"; Vast filter sidebar → offer cards; Akash filtered table → console bids; SF windows → quote/depth), while vendors present a static rate card with "Get started" / "Contact sales" (RunPod, Together, CoreWeave).

Visual language splits by business model: marketplaces and exchanges are dark-themed and mono-heavy (SF Compute ABC Diatype/ABC Diatype Mono, Prime Intellect IBM Plex Mono, Together PP Neue Montreal Mono, Akash JetBrains Mono, RunPod ABC Diatype, Vast Roboto on #0a0a0a); CoreWeave alone is a light corporate theme (Plus Jakarta Sans, blue #0541e9). Segmented toggles (Secure/Community, Per hour/Per second, 30D/90D, region) are the common control for switching price context.
Billing granularity is marketed as a price feature: Vast per-second, RunPod per-second toggle, SF Compute whole-minute fills with 1 node x 1 minute minimum; the vendor cards bill hourly.

cross_cutting: Every serious data page prints an update timestamp with its time zone next to the numbers and a separate delay statement: CME 'Last Updated 15 Sep 2026 11:55:00 PM CT' + 'delayed by at least 10 minutes'; ICE 'Last Update Time … GMT' + 'As of … ET - Market data delayed minimum of 15 minutes'; EEX 'Last update: 2026-09-15 21:00 CET'; Nord Pool 'Updated at: 16.09.2026 12:05:22 (GMT/BST)' with a 'Final' status badge; FRED 'Updated: Sep 15, 2026 4:03 PM CDT' + 'Next Release Date'.

Settlement basis is shown as its own labelled quantity, never blended with last trade: CME has separate Last (with A/B bid-ask flags) and Settle columns and a caveat that no-OI settlements are 'not based on market activity'; EEX headlines 'Settlement Price' with an EOD/Intraday toggle; Euronext footnotes the 10h:30 OI cut-off; vendors state the snapshot (Argus 'New York 2:30pm timestamp', Treasury 'at or near 3:30 PM', ICE 19:28 two-minute window).

Exchanges present the curve as a tenor ladder table in delivery order rather than a chart; ICE interleaves months, quarters, seasons and calendar strips chronologically, CME lists monthly rows with a 'Load All' expander, EEX exposes one contract at a time. Cross-tenor curve charts are a third-party/terminal feature (TradingView, Barchart Trader, Koyfin).

Yield-curve tools default to ordinal tenor ticks (1M 2M 3M 4M 6M 1Y 2Y 3Y 5Y 7Y 10Y 20Y 30Y on TradingView; 1 Mo…30 Yr columns on Treasury) and offer a switch to a time-proportional axis ('linear or a tenor scale' on TradingView); ustreasuryyieldcurve states 'duration in months or years'; Barchart Trader plots against the contract's expiration date.

Historical comparison is done by overlaying dated curves with an explicit 'On date' label per line: TradingView defaults to Current / 1 month ago / 1 year ago and clones a curve to change its date; Koyfin allows up to ten curves across dates and countries with per-line colour/width/style and data labels; ustreasuryyieldcurve uses a Pin button plus a date slider; StockCharts scrubs and animates with a trail; CME STIR compares to the previous settle; CurveWatch shows 1D/1W/1M changes; EIA overlays three dated curves with a date legend.

A data table always accompanies the curve chart and often doubles as the legend: TradingView rows beneath the chart with per-curve checkbox and optional heatmap mode; Koyfin table alongside; FRED 'View as data table'; Platts 'charts or table format'.

No exchange, government or vendor page labels contango/backwardation or inversion on the chart itself; shape labelling appears only in explanatory prose (EIA, TradingView/worldgovernmentbonds FAQs) or community indicators (TradingView Pine scripts). Spreads are used as the numeric shape cue instead (FRED T10Y2Y, worldgovernmentbonds 2s10s in bp, CurveWatch 2YY-10Y).

Units and change conventions are printed at the header/axis and change is shown in both absolute and percent or in the same unit as the level: EEX 'Settlement Price: 130.15 EUR/MWh ( -5.65 EUR/MWh )', Barchart '102.93 -2.90 (-2.74%)', TradingView Chg and Chg% columns, FRED 'Percent, Not Seasonally Adjusted'.

Methodology/provenance lives in a block adjacent to the data rather than a separate site: FRED Notes + Suggested Citation, Treasury methodology paragraph and link on the data page, Fed 'staff research product' disclaimer above the CSV, CME 'About this Report', Argus PDF with zero-arbitrage rule and corrections policy, Platts 'it is not a forecast', StockCharts/TradingView vendor credits in the footer.

Strip consistency is stated as a rule where curves are modelled: Argus 'the price of a strip product will always be equal to the average of the component periods'; ICE lists quarter/season/calendar strips beside their component months; Nord Pool shows block prices (Off-peak 1 / Peak / Off-peak 2) with Min/Max/Average under the granular table.

Controls cluster into: a date picker (calendar with Today/Clear/Go/Reset on EEX; last-5-sessions dropdown on CME; slider with arrows on ustreasuryyieldcurve), a product/tenor selector (multi-select month chips on Euronext; Key tenors toggle on TradingView; product-code picker on EEX), range buttons on time series (1Y/5Y/10Y/Max on FRED; Intraday/3M/1Y/2Y on ICE), and layer checkboxes (Settl. Price/Volume/OI on EEX; Fed Funds/CPI/TIPS on ustreasuryyieldcurve; Recession shading on FRED).

Sharing and export are state-preserving: FRED Custom Graph Link/Embed/Image Link, StockCharts Permalink, ustreasuryyieldcurve 'Link to this specific chart', TradingView and Koyfin snapshot/PNG, Treasury CSV/XML, Nord Pool Export Excel.

Freemium gating targets depth and polish, not the headline: CME analytics and Koyfin/Montel/Argus/Platts UIs behind login or paywall; EEX limits the public window to 45 days; ustreasuryyieldcurve sells dark mode; TradingView sells real-time data while keeping delayed pages public.

functionality: Index card: 'H100 SXM price index', updated timestamp, headline '$2.53 per H100 hour'; segment toggle Compute | Tokens
Range tabs '1W 1M 3M 1Y ALL' above the chart; 'Compare with' dropdown; 'Save CSV' button; chart placeholder text 'No chart data available' / 'Loading chart…' before hydration
Table 'Daily Settled GPU Prices' with columns GPU, Price ($/GPU-hr), Settled, Detail (links to per-GPU market pages such as /markets/h100-sxm)
Navigation: Home, Analytics (GPU, Models, Power, Memory), Map, News, Documentation, Get Full Access; methodology page with 'Download PDF' and changelog

Governance features: validation flags before publication, restatement policy, Market Disruption Event fallback (carry-forward then suspension), Oversight Committee of 3-5 with independent majority, complaints procedure, IOSCO alignment statement
products.method_and_provenance: Each index is 'the volume-weighted winsorized mean of executed transaction prices for a given GPU type over a rolling one-hour window'. Winsorization bounds are symmetric percentiles (alpha, 1-alpha) of the volume-weighted empirical CDF; alpha 'is set by Ornn and is not published'. No trade-size minimum; no smoothing across windows. Eligibility: verified counterparties (anti wash-trade), GPU specs (CUDA version, VRAM) verified at onboarding and at clearing, periodic provider re-verification, only realised rental prices (offers excluded). Provider identities undisclosed. Conflict acknowledged: Ornn also operates a compute marketplace; affiliated venue trades get no preferential treatment and their share is monitored. Freshness shown as 'Updated <date> at 20:00 UTC' on the card and a 'Settled' date column; trade counts and window volumes are not shown publicly.

Pairing of a humanist/grotesk sans for UI with a monospace for code or numbers: Inter Variable + Berkeley Mono (Linear), Geist Sans + Geist Mono (Vercel), Inter + Roboto Mono (Grafana), sohne-var + SourceCodePro (Stripe), PP Neue Montreal + Geist Mono (Ornn), MetricWeb + Financier display (FT).

Colour palettes are constructed in perceptual spaces: Linear LCH (base/accent/contrast), Stripe CIELAB with a 'levels apart' contrast rule, Vercel tokens declared in lab() and oklch(), Datawrapper HCL picker, Ornn Tailwind lab() fallbacks.

Hierarchy through weight and size rather than colour: Linear 510/590 medium/semibold, Grafana bold capped at 500, Stripe six sizes/weights with light 300 display; hero figures in Ornn use a serif (FK Roman Standard) to separate them from body text.

Index and metric pages state unit, freshness and method next to the headline number: Ornn shows '$2.53 per H100 hour', 'Updated September 15, 2026 at 20:00 UTC', a Settled date column and a one-sentence methodology in the footer; Datawrapper's anatomy is title, description, plot, notes, source, byline; FT vocabulary cards carry name, 'good for' line and example.

Range and comparison controls sit in a compact toolbar directly above or top-right of the main chart: Ornn '1W 1M 3M 1Y ALL' + 'Compare with' + 'Save CSV'; Vercel timeframe and environment dropdowns top-right; Linear Insights selectors above the graph with filters in a right sidebar; Grafana panel options in a right-hand editor.

A detail table sits beneath the chart and every product offers CSV export: Ornn 'Daily Settled GPU Prices' table + Save CSV; Linear Insights data table + Export to CSV; Vercel panels + 'Export as CSV' (250 rows); Stripe reports CSV/PDF/Excel.

Thin or missing data is handled by explicit gaps and dashed styles rather than interpolation by default: Grafana 'Connect null values: Never' default, Dash/Dots line styles, 'No value' default '-'; Datawrapper 'Connect all points' is an opt-in toggle; Ornn's methodology defines carry-forward and suspension for Market Disruption Events but shows no on-chart flag.

Uncertainty is drawn as a low-opacity band in the series colour: Observable Plot linearRegression ci 0.95 at fillOpacity 0.1, bollinger at 0.2; Datawrapper 'Add area fill' between two lines; Grafana thresholds as dashed lines or filled regions; FT lists fan charts as a standard Change-over-Time form.

Previous-period comparison is shown as a smaller secondary figure next to the headline: Stripe home metrics (current vs previous period in smaller text, per third-party breakdown), Ornn 1/7/30-day deltas and 'Compare with', Vercel timeframe-relative panels.

Direct labelling beats legends in the editorial references: Datawrapper right-aligned line labels with connector lines, Plot selectLast text marks with white halo, Bloomberg-style guides put labels adjacent to data; Grafana (legend bottom by default) is the dashboard-tool exception.

Provenance and governance are published as prose pages with dated changelogs where the data is a benchmark: Ornn methodology (24 Jul 2026, PDF + changelog, IOSCO statement, conflicts section); the design systems mirror this with versioned token packages (o-colors -> o3-foundation, Geist, Saga).
